key_insight: In photonic hybrid quantum neural networks, hardware noise can sometimes function as a built-in regularizer, improving accuracy on some datasets instead of only degrading performance.
engineering_relevance: This suggests quantum photonic hardware may reduce the need for explicit regularization in some workloads, but the benefit is dataset- and configuration-dependent.
method: Built PHQCNN models in Quandela Perceval with the MerLin framework.
Injected Perceval’s seven-parameter physical noise model directly during training.
Used a genetic algorithm to search noise settings and compare them against a noiseless baseline.
evidence_signal: Across five seeds, GA-tuned noise improved validation accuracy on Iris (+0.82 pp) and Digits (+1.45 pp) but reduced performance on MNIST (-1.21 pp).
watch_item: No single noise parameter was consistently helpful, so the regularization effect is not universal and requires joint tuning per dataset.
paper_title: PN-QNN: Harnessing Physical Noise as a Native Regularizer in Photonic Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks
